$comment: Canonical non-verb root fields for schema/verbs.json. Edit this file and the ordered verb fragments, then run node scripts/generate-verbs.mjs.

root.$comment: ShellX Cut verb registry — the public contract. Single source of truth: the server loads this file, MCP tools are generated from it (dots→underscores), the typed UI client mirrors it, and the coverage gate asserts REST and MCP both expose 100% of these verbs. Envelope: {ok, result?, op_ids?, project_revision?, warnings?[], error?{code,message,clip_id?,at_ms?,cause,suggested_action?}}. Optional mutation_controls are merged into every live verb input schema: op-emitting calls persist request identity, enforce expected_revision atomically, and replay completed lost-response retries. Warnings carry non-fatal guardrail findings in-band rather than only in logs. File-writing verbs such as render.final{path} and export.*{path} fence output paths through canonicalization, traversal and symlink rejection, allowed roots, and suffix allowlists. REST path = POST /api/verb/{name}.

request_id.description: Caller-generated retry identity. For an op-emitting mutation, the same caller + request_id + payload returns the original durable response; a changed payload conflicts.

expected_revision.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard. Requires request_id and must match the current durable project_revision when the first op commits.

project_revision.description: Latest durable operation ID after a successful project mutation

warnings.description: Non-fatal guardrail findings (e.g. preflight fps/resolution auto-conform). Integrity violations hard-error instead.

events.$comment: WS stream at GET /api/events (public verb contract 'events'). Every message: {type,...payload}. Ordering guarantee : receipt_ready always follows render_done — agents key on receipt_ready. receipt_ready is RE-EMITTED when verify.judge attaches its review (no separate judge event type: the second emission is distinguishable by receipt.judge presence).
